## Executive Summary

The CurseForge App is the highest-market-share third-party launcher, owned by Overwolf, and
proprietary — studied strictly black-box per ADR-0002: its published Core API, its documented
modpack formats, its author-facing policies, and the on-disk layout of our own legitimate
installation. Three things make it strategically important to Omni beyond market share.
First, its **content platform policies** are load-bearing constraints for Phase 6/7: the Core
API requires issued keys, mod authors can opt out of third-party API distribution per project,
and author monetization (points from downloads) means Omni must route downloads through the
official API so authors keep earning — all of which COMPLIANCE.md §5 already encodes. Second,
its **formats are de-facto standards**: the manifest.json modpack format and per-instance
minecraftinstance.json are what hundreds of thousands of packs and instances exist in — Omni's
importers must read both flawlessly (our own machine's install provides legitimate samples).
Third, its **auth posture** is the compliance reference the director explicitly named: login
is the standard Microsoft OAuth chain — the same documented chain specified in COMPLIANCE.md
§2 and verified in open source in the prism-launcher dossier.

## Architecture Components

### Instance store (observed layout)

- **Location**: `%USERPROFILE%/curseforge/minecraft/Instances/<instance>/`
- **Role**: Self-contained instance folders with a JSON descriptor over .minecraft-style content
- **Sources**: `local-install`, `cf-support`

Each instance is a folder containing minecraftinstance.json (instance descriptor: game
version, modloader coordinates, installed addon list with project/file IDs) beside standard
game content (mods/, config/, saves/…). Functionally the same self-contained-instance model
MultiMC pioneered, with platform identity (project/file IDs) embedded per mod — the same
mod-as-entity grain ATLauncher models. Omni's importer reads these folders in place; the IDs
make re-resolution against the Core API straightforward.

### Core API platform surface

- **Location**: `api.curseforge.com (documented at docs.curseforge.com)`
- **Role**: The published content API: search, files, fingerprints, categories — key-gated
- **Sources**: `cf-api-docs`

Documented REST surface requiring an issued API key: game/category browsing, mod search,
file metadata with hashes and dependencies, and MurmurHash2 fingerprint matching (the hash
family behind 'identify this local jar' — the counterpart of the mechanism the prism dossier
documents). Rate limits and key terms apply; per-project distribution opt-outs are enforced
at this API (files of opted-out projects are not served to third parties). Omni's Phase 6
census client must implement key management, honor opt-outs, and never circumvent via
scraping (COMPLIANCE.md §5).

## Feature Inventory

### mod-platforms

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Per-project third-party distribution opt-out | core | 4/5 | adopt | `cf-3rd-party`, `cf-api-docs` |
| Author monetization via download points | core | 4/5 | adopt | `cf-support`, `cf-eternal` |
| Fingerprint-based local file identification | core | 4/5 | adopt | `cf-api-docs` |

**Per-project third-party distribution opt-out** — Authors control whether their files are served to third-party apps via the Core API.

*Omni notes*: A hard legal/ethical constraint on Phase 6/7: the census marks opted-out projects; Omni surfaces 'get it in the official app' paths instead of circumventing.

**Author monetization via download points** — Downloads through official channels earn authors revenue points.

*Omni notes*: Omni routes all CurseForge downloads through the official API so author earnings are preserved — already encoded in COMPLIANCE.md §5; the census should track this as part of author-relations posture for Phase 7 outreach.

**Fingerprint-based local file identification** — MurmurHash2 fingerprints resolve unknown local jars to platform identities via the API.

*Omni notes*: Converges with the prism hash-recovery finding; Omni's census bootstraps user libraries with both platforms' hash APIs.

### instance-model

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| manifest.json modpack format | core | 4/5 | adopt | `cf-api-docs`, `cf-support` |

**manifest.json modpack format** — The platform's pack interchange: manifest with modloader + file ID list + overrides folder.

*Omni notes*: One of the three modpack lingua francas (with .mrpack and mmc-pack); importer required.

## Authentication Flows

### Microsoft account login (documented posture)

Public documentation describes standard Microsoft account sign-in for Minecraft — the same
OAuth chain COMPLIANCE.md §2 specifies and the prism-launcher dossier verifies in source.
No password handling by the app; consent in Microsoft's surfaces. This is the 'handle login
the same way CurseForge does' reference the director set: implement the documented MSA chain,
nothing more.

Steps:

1. Microsoft OAuth (documented consumer flow) -> 2. Xbox Live/XSTS -> 3. Minecraft services
token + entitlement/profile (documented chain; see prism-launcher dossier for the
source-verified step detail Omni implements)

*Sources*: `cf-support`, `cf-api-docs`

## File Formats

### minecraftinstance.json (json)

- **Path pattern**: `%USERPROFILE%/curseforge/minecraft/Instances/<name>/minecraftinstance.json`
- **Sources**: `local-install`

Per-instance descriptor observed in our legitimate install: game version, modloader
identity/version, and the installed addon list with platform project/file IDs and metadata.
Omni's importer treats it as authoritative for re-resolving the instance against the Core
API (exact field semantics to be captured from our own instances during importer work,
Phase 4/5 — legitimately, from our own data).

### CurseForge modpack manifest.json (zip+json)

- **Path pattern**: `<pack>.zip: manifest.json + overrides/`
- **Sources**: `cf-api-docs`, `cf-support`

Documented pack format: manifest (manifestVersion, minecraft.version + modLoaders list,
name/author, files[] as projectID/fileID pairs with required flags) plus an overrides/ tree
copied into the instance. Importer required for Phase 4/5; export support decides later.

## Protocols & API Surfaces

### CurseForge Core API

- **Endpoint**: `https://api.curseforge.com (documented at docs.curseforge.com)`
- **Sources**: `cf-api-docs`

Key-gated REST API: games/categories, mod search, mod/file metadata (hashes, dependencies,
download URLs where permitted), and fingerprint matching. The Phase 6 census consumes it
within its terms: issued key, rate limits, opt-out honoring, no scraping.

## Analysis Notes

### ADR-0002 boundary statement

Everything above derives from public documentation, published API surfaces, and the layout of
our own legitimate installation. No decompilation, no traffic interception, no binary
inspection was performed or will be. Where field-level format semantics are needed (e.g.
minecraftinstance.json), they will be captured from our own instances' files — data we own —
during importer development.

*Sources*: `cf-api-docs`, `local-install`
